title: One-click Reject on an AI review card: no confirmation, silent candidate email, not in the reconsider undo
expected: Rejecting a candidate from an AI review card (irreversible, candidate-facing) asks for confirmation or previews the rendered rejection, confirms the send afterward, and offers a way back.
got: Live on the Decisions tab (cs), the AI recommendation cards render a bare 'Zamítnout' button (3 present on the seeded queue) with NO confirm step, NO rendered-message preview — one click applies + queues the rejection email. Confirmed by code (AiReviewCard.onReject → act(e,'reject') → POST /api/pipeline/[id] → dispatchRejection, no dialog) and by the visible card markup. Card/human rejects never enter the reconsider queue (auto_rejected-only) — cross-confirmed by the pipeline-advance L2. I did NOT click a seeded card (mutation discipline); the danger is the absence of a gate, visible without firing it.
evidence: cross-ref: marek-coordinator--pipeline-advance--L2.md (command/human reject → outbox, absent from reconsider)
suggested_acceptance: A card Reject shows a confirm step naming the candidate + the message that will be sent; after the send, an explicit confirmation; a mis-clicked card reject has a recall/reinstate path (or reconsider includes recent human rejects).
scope_note: The wave path (this journey's core) is exemplary; this finding is the single-card manual reject affordance beside it.

title: Never-scored candidate auto-rejected on a fabricated 'match 0' — and the fabricated figure is now sealed in the immutable chain
expected: A candidate with matchScore=null is excluded from the wave (or flagged 'unscored — needs review'); a sealed adverse record never asserts a measurement that was never taken.
got: I created a Screened entry with matchScore=null (archetype 'bau', so archetype-shielding does NOT save it), opened the wave: it appears in the would-reject list as 'match 0', rationale 'Would auto-reject · bottom 20% of 3 → 1 (rank 1) and match 0 < 45 threshold.' — indistinguishable from a genuine zero. On commit, a tamper-evident record sealed PERMANENTLY (chain verified OK, 27 links): EN rationale 'match 0 < 45', cs localized 'shoda 0 < práh 45', inputs.score:0. An adverse automated decision computed AND sealed on absent data.
evidence: live dry-run: entry matchScore=null rendered matchScore:0, action reject
suggested_acceptance: An entry with matchScore=null at Screened is excluded from the wave cohort (listed separately 'unscored — needs review') or visibly marked unscored in the preview; a sealed record never renders a null score as 0.

title: Auto-rejection email (both locales) has no automated-decision disclosure and no contest / human-review channel
expected: A candidate adversely affected by automated processing is told automation was involved and offered a route to request human intervention / contest (GDPR Art. 22(3) / AI Act transparency).
got: Read the live outbox bodies in BOTH locales. EN (auto-reject, pe-047 / my UAT fixtures): 'After careful review, we won't be moving forward at this stage.' cs (Martin Vondráček): 'Po pečlivém zvážení v tuto chvíli nebudeme pokračovat dál.' Neither discloses automated processing; neither offers a contest / human-review route. The template is identical for auto and manual rejects (dispatchRejection, no automated flag on the copy). The GDPR footer covers data access/erasure only. 'careful review' arguably misrepresents a threshold rule.
evidence: live dev_outbox rows: ref pe-047 (en), ref m-appl-martin-vondracek-...-job-043 (cs), ref m-uat-sd-null-uat-sd-l2job (en)
suggested_acceptance: The rejection comm for an auto-rejected candidate (automated:true) includes a plain-language automated-processing disclosure + a reply/link to request human re-review; the manual template stays as-is.

title: Sealed record of a human decision omits the AI recommendation it ratified — dossier can't show what the human saw
expected: When a recruiter accepts/rejects from an AI card, the sealed record captures what the AI recommended (verdict, confidence, rationale, model) so a right-to-explanation dossier shows machine input + human call.
got: Exported the live decision dossier (one click, 27 records). Every human 'advanced'/'rejected' record carries only inputs {fromStage, detail} — e.g. {'fromStage':'Hired','detail':null} — with NO model/verdict/confidence field anywhere in the payload (regex for model|confidence|recommendation|verdict = false). The AI recommendation lives in mutable approval_detail and is cleared on decision. For a human-ratified AI decision, the dossier still forces reconstruction of what the AI told the human — the exact threshold Lucie's motivation names.
evidence: uat/runs/2026-07-02-full/shots/sd-l2-dossier-export.json (advanced/rejected records: inputs = {fromStage, detail}; no AI payload)
suggested_acceptance: For an accept/reject on an entry carrying a *_review approval, the sealed inputs include the approval payload snapshot (recommendation, confidence, source/model); the candidate's dossier shows the AI input alongside the human decision.

title: approvedBy in the immutable record reads a generic constant ('operator (single-operator deployment)')
expected: The 'who approved this reviewed set' claim in a sealed Art. 22 record names an authenticated person.
got: The modal supplies no approvedBy, so the commit path falls to operatorApprover() → KP_OPERATOR_NAME is unset on this deployment → every one of my 3 committed wave rejects sealed 'approved by operator (single-operator deployment)'. Confirmed in the sealed records AND the exported dossier. The route also accepts any client-supplied approvedBy string with no identity check.
ceiling: Single-operator deployment with no per-user identity: a truly authenticated approver requires the multi-user auth layer; until then KP_OPERATOR_NAME is a deployment precondition and the client-supplied approvedBy should be dropped or bound to the session.
suggested_acceptance: The commit path derives approvedBy from the server-side session/env only (never the request body); a deployment without KP_OPERATOR_NAME gets a warning on the records panel.

title: Reinstate restores the pipeline but offers no follow-up, though the rejection email already went out
expected: Reinstating an auto-rejected candidate prompts (or reminds about) a follow-up — they were already told 'no' under the bank's name.
got: Live: expanded 'Znovu zvážit' (showed my 3 auto-rejected UAT fixtures), clicked Obnovit on 'UAT SD Alpha' → it left the queue and returned active@Screened (verified in DB; a 'reinstated' reversal sealed as seq 27). The UI showed NO reminder that a rejection letter already shipped and offered NO follow-up draft — the correction is invisible to the candidate unless the coordinator remembers.
evidence: DB: m-uat-sd-a → status active@Screened; decision_records seq 27 kind reinstated
ceiling: Auto-sending a 're-review' note is deliberately avoided (a reinstate may be exploratory); the gap is the missing affordance/nudge, not the auto-send.
suggested_acceptance: After Reinstate, the row/banner reminds a rejection note was delivered and offers a one-click localized follow-up draft.

title: Per-candidate decision dossier (?candidate=) works at the API but has no UI consumer — DSAR is export-all-and-filter
expected: A candidate-scoped 'view/export this subject's sealed record' affordance for right-to-explanation / DSAR.
got: Live: GET /api/decisions/records?candidate=m-uat-sd-null-... returns exactly that subject's 1 record (scoping works server-side). But the DecisionRecordsPanel on Analytics fetches unscoped and shows no candidate filter/scope control (checked live: hasCandidateScopeControl=false); export dumps the whole chain. No Decisions/Reconsider affordance links a candidate to their sealed records.
evidence: live: ?candidate= returns 1 scoped record; panel has no scope control (sd-l2-06-analytics-records)
suggested_acceptance: From the records panel (or candidate drawer) one click scopes to a single candidateRef and exports that subject's dossier; the chain verdict stays global with copy noting integrity is chain-wide.

title: AI screening card rationale/strengths render in English inside the Czech workspace
expected: The screening recommendation a Czech coordinator ratifies reads in Czech, like the wave's DEC4-localized rationales.
got: Live: a screening_review card (Hana Černá, pe-004) renders its rationale in English — 'Strong senior backend profile that the automated skills match under-scores...' — and English strengths, inside an otherwise fully-Czech Decisions tab. (Notably the scorecard cards were bilingual cs+EN; the screening card is English-only, matching the code: only 'prep' gets --lang.)
evidence: live: pe-004 approval_detail rationale English; sd-l2-01-decisions.png
suggested_acceptance: The screen task receives the workspace locale (mirroring prep) or the card renders a structured localized mirror.

title: Ship-bar: /api/decisions/* have no in-route auth or tenant scoping; the chain is workspace-less and served unauthenticated
expected: On the public product path, screen-wave commits, sealed records and the reconsider queue are session-authenticated and workspace-scoped.
got: UNAUTHENTICATED PROBE (fresh curl, no cookies, no dev gate): GET /api/decisions/records → HTTP 200 with all 26 sealed records (incl. real ČS candidate refs like m-cand-007-...) and chain.ok; POST /api/decisions/screen-wave dry-run → HTTP 200. In THIS dev deployment KP_OPERATOR_PASSWORD is unset so the proxy gate is off entirely. Code asymmetry: /api/automation/[task] calls requireOperator() (which even rejects anonymous demo sessions), but screen-wave/records/reconsider call NO in-route gate — so on the password-set multi-tenant path a demo/anonymous session that passes the proxy would still reach them, and decision_records has no workspace column (one global chain) → cross-tenant read of every candidate's adverse-action record.
suggested_acceptance: Decisions routes call requireOperator() (rejecting demo sessions) on the production path and every decision record carries + filters by workspace id.
scope_note: Ship-bar (public product path). Near-zero live impact in the current single-operator dev deployment; ranks below the every-run findings but is a hard must-fix before multi-tenant.

title: The reconsider queue shows a null-score reject with no score and no 'unscored' flag — even the undo surface can't tell it was rejected on a fabricated 0
expected: The one surface that lets a human catch/reverse a bad auto-reject flags a candidate who was rejected without a real score.
got: My auto-rejected null-score fixture ('UAT SD Null (unscored)') appears in the reconsider queue with the match line simply OMITTED (matchScore null → the '· shoda {score}' chip is not rendered), rather than an explicit 'unscored' marker. So neither the preview (shows 'match 0') nor the undo queue (shows blank) distinguishes a never-measured candidate from a genuine low scorer — the human gate SD-L1-002 relies on is blind on both ends.
suggested_acceptance: A null-score entry surfaces an explicit 'unscored' badge in both the wave preview and the reconsider row, so the missing measurement is visible where a human could act on it.

title: Strength (live): the Art.22 gate holds under real probing — 409 without a token, 409 on a stale token, zero mutation across previews, verified chain
got: Drove the real server path: dry-run at 3 slider positions returned 1/2/1 rejects (preview tracks the override live) with zero mutation (cohort stayed 4 active, 0 records, 0 outbox); commit with NO token → 409 'approval required'; commit with a stale token → 409 're-preview'; commit with the fresh token → applied exactly the previewed set. The tamper-evident chain re-verified OK across all 3 commits + a reinstate (27 links, brokenAtSeq null); the reversal sealed as its own link. Fairness shield fail-closed proven live: the job-004 wave 'would reject 0 of 3' because 2 students + 1 null-archetype are all shielded, with the shield note shown.
evidence: live: 409/409/200 token sequence on jobId uat-sd-l2job
chain verify ok:true count 27 after 3 commits + reinstate
ceiling: Records are best-effort (sealDecisionSafe never throws) — the chain is near-complete, not guaranteed-complete; human-decision records stay thin (SD-L1-004).
